mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, to be written and committed one after the other, each with its own tests:
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap to lines of at most `width` characters, words longer than the width on their own line; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits, otherwise cuts at the last word boundary that fits and appends "…", never exceeding `max` characters.
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes.
Record one design decision with the decision tool: how word boundaries are defined, since wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it. `npm test` must pass.

plan.summary: Add a new ESM module src/text.js exporting slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords, with node:test tests in test/text.test.js, delivered as a single worker task as requested. The worker writes and commits the functions one after the other (four commits, each containing one function plus its tests), and records exactly one design decision via the decision tool on how word boundaries are defined so that wrap, truncate and countWords agree. The repo is a tiny dependency-free ESM package (package.json: "type": "module", test script "node --test"; existing code in src/index.js and test/index.test.js uses single quotes and no semicolons), so no config or tooling changes are needed: node --test picks up test/text.test.js automatically.
assumptions: The single design decision is recorded by the worker during implementation (not by the planner), so exactly one decision record exists and it matches the code that ships.

Word-boundary definition to implement and record: a word character is a Unicode letter, a digit or an apostrophe (one shared pattern such as /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu); a word is a maximal run of word characters. countWords counts those runs. wrap and truncate only ever break at whitespace, which is never inside a word run, so neither function splits a word that countWords would count; punctuation stays attached to its adjacent word in the output.

wrap returns a single string with lines joined by "\n" (not an array); any run of whitespace in the input, including existing newlines, is treated as one separator; an empty or whitespace-only string yields "".
A word longer than width in wrap is placed on its own line unbroken, so that one line may exceed width; this is the only exception to the 'at most width' rule.
"Characters" means JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units) for both width and max.

truncate counts the "…" (a single character, U+2026) inside the max budget; trailing whitespace before the ellipsis is removed; if not even the first word fits within max - 1 characters, the text is hard-cut to max - 1 characters followed by "…".
truncate throws TypeError unless max is a positive integer, mirroring wrap, because the 'never exceed max' guarantee cannot be met otherwise. The request does not specify this.
wrap, truncate and countWords throw TypeError for a non-string text argument, consistent with slugify. The request only specifies this for slugify.
slugify's 'alphanumeric' means ASCII a-z and 0-9 after NFD decomposition and removal of combining marks; other characters become separators.
src/index.js is not changed (no re-export of the new functions), since the request only asks for src/text.js and its tests.
The worker is allowed to create git commits on the current branch (the request explicitly asks for each function to be committed in turn); nothing is pushed.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exists and exports exactly the four named functions slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords as ESM named exports.
test/text.test.js exists, uses node:test and node:assert/strict, and contains tests for each of the four functions.
`npm test` exits with code 0, with both test/index.test.js and test/text.test.js passing and no skipped or todo tests.
git log shows four new commits after e96371f, in the order slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords, each adding one function together with its tests, and `npm test` passes at each of those commits.
Exactly one design decision about the word-boundary definition has been recorded with the decision tool, and the behaviour of wrap, truncate and countWords matches it.
Only src/text.js and test/text.test.js are added; package.json, README.md, src/index.js and test/index.test.js are unchanged, and no dependencies are added.

tasks.title: Implement src/text.js (slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords) with tests, one commit per function
tasks.description:
Repository: a tiny dependency-free ESM package named textkit (package.json has "type": "module" and the script "test": "node --test"; Node v24 is installed). Existing files are src/index.js (exports VERSION) and test/index.test.js. Match their style: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, tests importing from '../src/<file>.js'. Platform is native Windows; do not rely on POSIX-only tools.

Create two new files: src/text.js and test/text.test.js. Do not modify package.json, README.md, src/index.js or test/index.test.js, and add no dependencies.

Work strictly in this order, and after each step run `npm test` and make a git commit containing just that function and its tests (four commits in total, on the current branch, no push). End each commit message with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Before writing wrap, record exactly ONE design decision with mcp__nexus__record_decision describing how word boundaries are defined, because wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it. Use this definition unless you find a concrete reason it cannot work (if so, record the definition you actually implement, still as one single decision): a word character is a Unicode letter, a digit or an apostrophe; a word is a maximal run of word characters, expressed as one shared module-level pattern (for example /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu) used by countWords. wrap and truncate break only at whitespace, which is never inside a word run, so they never split a word that countWords counts; punctuation stays attached to its neighbouring word in the output. Do not record any other decision.

1. slugify(text): throw TypeError when text is not a string. Lower-case, normalize with NFD and strip combining diacritical marks, replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters (anything other than a-z and 0-9) with a single "-", then trim "-" from both ends. Tests: plain phrase, diacritics (e.g. 'Crème Brûlée' -> 'creme-brulee'), runs of mixed punctuation and spaces collapsing to one "-", leading/trailing separators trimmed, empty string and all-punctuation input -> '', non-string arguments (number, null, undefined) throw TypeError. Commit.

2. wrap(text, width): throw TypeError unless width is a positive integer (reject 0, negatives, non-integers, NaN, numeric strings) and when text is not a string. Greedy word wrap: split on whitespace runs, pack as many words per line as fit with single spaces so each line is at most width characters, and put a word longer than width on its own line unbroken. Return one string with lines joined by "\n"; empty or whitespace-only input returns ''. Tests: text shorter than width unchanged, a multi-line wrap with exact expected output, a line that fits exactly at width, an over-long word on its own line between normal lines, multiple spaces/newlines in the input collapsed, empty input, every line of a normal wrap being <= width, invalid widths throw TypeError. Commit.

3. truncate(text, max): throw TypeError when text is not a string or max is not a positive integer. Return text unchanged when text.length <= max. Otherwise cut at the last word boundary (whitespace position) such that the kept part, with trailing whitespace removed, plus "…" (single character U+2026) is at most max characters, and append "…". If not even the first word fits, hard-cut to max - 1 characters and append "…". The result must never exceed max characters. Tests: text that fits returned unchanged, text of exactly max length unchanged, cut at a word boundary with exact expected output, no trailing space before the ellipsis, a cut that would land mid-word backing off to the previous word, a single over-long word hard-cut, max of 1 yielding '…', result length <= max across several max values, invalid max throws TypeError. Commit.

4. countWords(text): throw TypeError when text is not a string. Return the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes (the shared pattern). Tests: empty string and whitespace/punctuation-only -> 0, a simple sentence, apostrophes inside words counted as one word ("don't stop" -> 2), digits counted ('route 66' -> 2), hyphen and other punctuation separating words ('well-known' -> 2), accented letters counted as part of a word, plus at least one test showing agreement with wrap and truncate: the countWords total of a text equals the sum over the lines produced by wrap, and a truncated result does not end in a partial word of the original. Commit.

Do not hard-code behaviour to satisfy tests, and leave no temporary files behind. Finish by running `npm test` and `git status` / `git log --oneline` and report the real output.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exports the named functions slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords and nothing else is required to import them (`import { slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords } from './src/text.js'` works).
slugify('  Crème Brûlée!! ') returns 'creme-brulee', slugify('--a  b__c--') returns 'a-b-c', and slugify(42) throws TypeError.
wrap('the quick brown fox', 10) returns 'the quick\nbrown fox'; a word longer than width appears alone on its own line; wrap('a b', 0), wrap('a b', 1.5) and wrap('a b', '5') throw TypeError.
truncate('hello world', 11) returns 'hello world'; truncate('hello brave new world', 12) returns 'hello brave…'; for every tested max the result length is <= max.
countWords("don't stop, route 66") returns 4 and countWords('') returns 0.

test/text.test.js contains tests for all four functions, including a test that wrap, truncate and countWords agree on word boundaries, and `npm test` exits 0 with all tests in test/index.test.js and test/text.test.js passing.
git log shows four new commits after e96371f in the order slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords, each touching only src/text.js and test/text.test.js, and the working tree is clean at the end.
Exactly one decision about the word-boundary definition was recorded with mcp__nexus__record_decision, and the implemented behaviour matches it.
package.json, README.md, src/index.js and test/index.test.js are unchanged.

risks.description: The word definition for countWords (runs of letters, digits, apostrophes) and whitespace-based breaking in wrap/truncate could be implemented as unrelated rules that drift apart, e.g. on hyphenated or punctuated text.
risks.mitigation: The task fixes one definition up front, requires a single shared pattern in the module, a recorded decision, and an explicit cross-function agreement test.

risks.description: Off-by-one errors in truncate around the ellipsis budget (result exceeding max, or a trailing space before "…"), especially for very small max or a first word longer than max.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance criteria and tests cover exact-fit, max of 1, over-long first word, and a length <= max check across several max values.

risks.description: Several behaviours are not specified by the request (wrap return type, truncate's validation of max, non-string text in wrap/truncate/countWords), so the chosen behaviour may differ from what the requester expected.
risks.mitigation: Each choice is listed in the assumptions and encoded in tests, so it is visible and cheap to change in one place if the requester disagrees.

risks.description: The four-commit requirement could be collapsed into one commit, or a commit could be made with failing tests.
risks.mitigation: The task orders the work explicitly, requires `npm test` before each commit, and the verifier checks git log for four ordered commits.

risks.description: Unicode property escapes or the literal "…" character could be mangled by file encoding on Windows.
risks.mitigation: Files are written as UTF-8; Node v24 supports \p{L}/\p{N} with the u flag, and tests assert on the exact ellipsis character and on accented input.
